Read the syllabus properly and set up Gradescope access

entries.what: First office hour. Two students, both about the setup instructions
Office hours, five students, all on the same install problem
entries.note: Five people with the identical error. That is a documentation problem, not five student problems.

entries.what: First discussion section I have run on my own
entries.note: I talked for forty minutes of fifty. Nobody asked anything. I do not think that means they understood.

entries.what: Wrote the install fix up as an Ed post and pinned it
Discussion section. Tried asking a question and waiting
entries.note: Waited about four seconds and it felt like a minute. Someone answered. Four seconds is apparently the whole trick.

entries.what: Office hours before the homework 2 deadline. Full the whole time
entries.note: Almost everyone opens with 'my code does not work' and nothing else. I spend the first five minutes of every conversation extracting what they already tried.

entries.what: Homework 2. Took five hours and I am not confident it is consistent
entries.note: The rubric says 'partial credit where appropriate' for the recursion question. That is not a rubric. I made a different call at 9pm than I made at 2pm and I cannot defend either.

entries.what: Regrade requests from homework 2, eleven of them
entries.note: Every single regrade was on the recursion question. That is the rubric, not the students.

entries.what: Staff meeting. Raised the homework 2 rubric problem
entries.note: Said it out loud with the numbers: five hours, eleven regrades, all on one question. Having the number made it a scheduling problem rather than me complaining.

entries.what: Rewrote the recursion rubric line with the instructor. Three checkable sub-points instead of 'where appropriate'
entries.note: Took forty minutes together. Should have happened before homework 2 went out.

entries.what: Office hours. Started asking 'what have you tried' before looking at any code
entries.note: Two sessions ended with the student finding it themselves. Both said thanks in a way they do not when I find it.

entries.what: Homework 3, finished. Two hours against five for homework 2
entries.note: Same size assignment. The difference is entirely the rubric. That is the clearest evidence I have that the fix worked.

entries.what: Practice problems for the midterm review
Extra office hours before the midterm. Nonstop
entries.note: Nobody asked a conceptual question all session. All of it was 'is this on the exam'.

entries.what: Midterm grading, my two questions across 120 papers
Midterm grading, second pass on the borderline scripts
entries.note: Third time I have changed my mind on the same answer. I should have graded question by question instead of paper by paper, and I knew that and did it anyway because it felt slower.

entries.what: Office hours, very quiet after the midterm
Discussion section, went over the midterm
Office hours. Kept using the 'what have you tried' opener
entries.note: I am getting through more students per session than in September and staying later with fewer of them. Both at once, which I did not expect.

entries.note: I nearly said 'of course, this is between us'. The reason I did not is that we covered it in week one. I would have got that wrong in September.

entries.note: Most of them are design questions that would be a five minute conversation and are a twenty minute thread. I should be pushing these to office hours.

Ed. The FAQ has visibly cut the repeats

entries.what: Final project rubric read-through with the instructor
entries.note: Asked for the rubric two weeks early this time. That is the homework 2 lesson, applied.

entries.what: Wrote up the install fix and the FAQ for whoever TAs this next
Final office hours before the exam
Handover notes for next semester's TA
entries.note: Reading back through this, the thing I would tell them is the homework 2 week. Not that it was bad, but that having it written down is what let me fix it in week five instead of complaining about it in December.

syllabus.note: Attendance in section is not graded, which surprises people who assume it is. Late work loses 10% a day up to three days and is then a zero, and the instructor will not make exceptions by email, only in person.

ai.note: Students may use AI to explain a concept or to help debug code they wrote. They may not submit code they did not write, and anything AI-assisted has to be declared in a comment at the top of the file. Undeclared use is an academic honesty referral, not a grade penalty.

late.note: 10% a day for three days, then zero. I do not have authority to extend anything. If someone asks me, I send them to the instructor and tell the instructor it is coming so it is not a surprise.

regrade.note: Within one week, through Gradescope, and it re-opens the whole question rather than just the part they queried. I regrade it, and if the change is more than two points the instructor reviews it.

honesty.note: I do not confront the student. I screenshot what I saw, email the instructor the same day, and say nothing to anyone else including the other TAs. The instructor decides whether it goes to Academic Honesty.

accom.note: The letters go to the instructor, not to me. What reaches me is an instruction, usually extended time or a separate room for quizzes in section. I implement it and do not assess it. If a student tells me about one I have not been told about, I believe them and check with the instructor afterwards rather than in front of them.

report.note: I am a responsible employee. If a student starts telling me about harassment or assault I have to report it, so I say that before they get into it rather than after. The Dean of Students and the counselling centre are the confidential routes, and I keep those two links to hand.

duties.note: Six hours: two of office hours Tuesday and Thursday, one discussion section Wednesday, grading within four days of a deadline, Ed answered within 24 hours on weekdays, and the Monday staff meeting. Agreed in writing in week one and it has held all term.

space.note: LGRT T222, booked through the Zoom booking system for Tuesday and Thursday 2 to 3. Keypad code from CSB-W126, and I had to sign the sheet there before they would give it to me.

staff.note: The instructor, a head UCA, two other grad TAs and three UCAs. Slack for anything quick between staff, Ed for anything a student might also need to see, email for anything that should be on the record.

weeks.flag: Still finding my feet. Section is the part I am worst at.

Homework 2 took five hours instead of the two I planned for, and produced eleven regrades, all on the same question. The rubric line for it is 'partial credit where appropriate', which is not something I can apply consistently. I want to agree it with the instructor before homework 3.
Still catching up from last week, but the rubric conversation happened and we rewrote the line together.
Homework 3 took half the time of homework 2 for the same size assignment. The rubric was the whole difference.
Midterm week. Twelve hours. This was known in advance and I agreed it with the instructor, so it is not a surprise, but it is worth recording that midterm week costs roughly a week and a half.
Quiet week after the midterm. It roughly balances the week before.
One difficult conversation in office hours that I handled by the book. Told the instructor the same day.
The project has doubled Ed volume. Two hours of it this week, mostly design questions that belong in office hours.
The project FAQ has cut the repeat questions sharply.
Finals week. Eleven hours. Same shape as the midterm, and again agreed in advance.
